retracted.reason: RETRACTED 2026-11-04. This verdict was not a comparison of anything. The candidate was measured at 19:29 and gated against a baseline measured at 18:41 - 48 minutes earlier, under a different set of resident processes. The difference between the two numbers described two different machine states, and was charged to the candidate. No statistical gate could have caught it: Welch's t-test on two independent series attributes the drift to the candidate, which is exactly what 'independent' means. Re-measured on 2026-11-04 with both arms alternately in one session (harness/levers.py, husk_threads lever), the same change is DENY -0.89% - it was never a win.

replacement_history.superseded_because: RE-MEASURED 2026-11-05 at 05:52, with the WSL-aware contention detector and the per-repetition quiet gate that the husk_threads lever had been MISSING (it was the one lever with no quiet_check - the lever that produced the phantom was also the one with the least protection). Both arms measured alternately in one session on a card verified idle by process identity: DENY, -0.60% (paired, n=5/5, baseline drift -0.28%, baseline cv 0.25%, zero contention events, ssim guardrail baseline 0.9964 vs candidate 0.9951). The 11:11 figure was -0.89% at +1.96% drift; this one is -0.60% at -0.28% drift. Both are DENY, and the effect is indistinguishable from zero either way: the default thread count and -j 48 are the same thing on a 48-thread box, so the difference that IS visible between repetitions (-0.74%, +0.09%, +0.13%, +0.19%, +4.0% across the five pairs) is the renderer's own run-to-run noise, not the thread count. The +12.34% this verdict reported was drift between sessions and was never a win.
